source.title: Seeing but Not Thinking: Routing Distraction in Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts
source.authors: Haolei Xu; Hai-Wen Hong; Hong-Xing Li; Rui Zhou; Yang Zhang; Long-Tao Huang; Hui Xue; Yong-Liang Shen; Weiming Lu; Yue-Ting Zhuang

page_placements.theme: Within-model modality and view correspondence has architecture-specific depth profiles

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-modal semantic sharing in a multimodal MoE using hidden-state concept intervention, a different method from measuring representational similarity or distance. It does not test whether alignment increases with model scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The cross-modal concept-intervention results in §3.1 bear on V2. The routing-divergence, expert-specialization, reasoning-accuracy, and routing-guidance results do not measure representational convergence and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version of the claim. Its only representational result (§3.1) patches text-derived concept vectors into image-token hidden states inside one jointly trained VLM, Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B. This measures within-model sharing across modalities, not alignment between separately trained vision and language models (V2). It also compares no models, scales or capability levels, so it says nothing about convergence rising as models improve (V1, V2). The intervention has no stated control baseline. The rest of the paper concerns MoE routing and accuracy. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis is cited once in related work. The finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the MoE VLM shows cross-modal semantic sharing in middle layers for simple digit concepts, so alignment failure alone does not explain 'Seeing but Not Thinking'. They propose Routing Distraction instead: image inputs cause routing divergence in middle layers, where domain experts concentrate, and this correlates with lower reasoning accuracy. Soft routing guidance improves accuracy across three MoE models, by up to 3.17%.
record.recipe_differences: Uses hidden-state concept substitution and intervention success, rather than comparing representational distances across independently trained models or scales.
record.method_sensitivity: Cross-modal intervention success varies by layer: it is low early, exceeds 90% in layers 8–42, and declines in terminal layers.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B, replacing a digit's text-derived hidden-state vector with another digit's vector in image-token states changes the arithmetic answer in over 90% of 100 instances in layers 8–42. Success is low in early layers and declines sharply in terminal layers (inverted U).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a single jointly trained VLM, image and text inputs share concept representations in middle layers, so text-derived concept vectors can steer image-token representations.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The alignment experiment uses simple numerical concepts in one model; it does not compare model scales or capabilities. Exact success rates outside the middle-layer range are not stated, and the text does not report uncertainty for these results.
record.rows_left_out: §3.2–§5 report expert specialization, routing divergence, reasoning accuracy, and routing-guidance outcomes; these do not measure representational convergence. Figure 3(b–c) and related tables are therefore not included as rows.

untested.parts: All: no comparison of independently trained models across scale or capability.
All: no alignment between separate vision and language models on paired data, and no trend with model quality. The within-model patching result is a different construct.
All: no cross-model mapping or stitching.
All: no features or circuits compared across models.
All: no similarity-metric or input-distribution sensitivity analysis of convergence.
All: no cross-model alignment levels, plateaus or causes examined.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V2 labels are withdrawn. The patching experiment is within one model, with no capability comparison and no control baseline, so it does not bear on V2 as stated. The authors themselves note it covers only simple numerical concepts. Venue: the record lists ACL, but the text shows only an arXiv preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Whether independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data become more aligned as scale and capability increase.

Whether alignment rises as both models improve; comparisons across models or model scales; paired image-caption representations. The experiment tests cross-modal semantic sharing for simple numerical concepts within one model.
Convergence across random seeds, shared features or subspaces, and differences between units or bases.
Whether representations can be mapped between models by a simple map, stitching, relative representations, or without paired data.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Whether convergence depends on similarity metric, metric settings, or input distribution.
Whether convergence is incomplete or plateaus across models, or whether shared training data or objectives explain it.

relation.reason: §2 cites Huh et al. (2024) on cross-modal convergence. The study's own experiments concern semantic sharing within a jointly trained VLM and routing distraction.

tranche.reason: Within-model cross-modal digit interventions do not test any listed claim version; no alignment comparison across independently trained models or capability levels is reported.

source_check.notes: The qualitative values in r1 and r3 are explicitly stated in §3.1 prose, despite their figure_only tags. The authors limit the semantic-sharing evidence to simple numerical concepts; complex visual concepts remain untested.
